title: Investigating Thinking Behaviours of Reasoning-Based Language Models for Social Bias Mitigation
benchmark_measurement: The benchmarks measured social bias, specifically stereotype detection and mitigation, in religious contexts as one of several demographic categories. This included evaluating model performance on ambiguous and unambiguous question-answering tasks and open-ended text generation involving religion.
findings: The paper found that its proposed prompt-based mitigation method, which guides a model to review its reasoning for stereotype repetition and irrelevant information, successfully reduced social bias and improved accuracy for the 'Religion' category across multiple benchmarks (BBQ, StereoSet, BOLD). Performance on the religion category was comparable to other social categories studied, showing that the identified failure patterns and mitigation strategies are generalizable. For instance, in the StereoSet benchmark (ambiguous contexts), the method improved accuracy and lowered bias scores for the Religion category on both tested models.
